# Table display witnesses

The expected strings come from the owner's declared display rule: values with magnitude at least 1e6, or nonzero magnitude below 1e-4, use four significant digits in scientific notation. Values at 1e-4 and zero remain plain. The scientific value keeps its display precision as a narrow cell clips its end. The supplied background value 22900000 with s.u. 100000 must display as `2.290e7` and `0.010e7`; editing shows `22900000`.

| Supplied value | Display |
| --- | --- |
| 999999 | 999999 |
| 1000000 | 1.000e6 |
| 0.0001 | 0.0001 |
| 0.00009999 | 9.999e-5 |
| 0 | 0 |
| -1000000 | -1.000e6 |
| -0.00001 | -1.000e-5 |
| 22900000 | 2.290e7 |

The project is the small, independently supplied message-wrapping project with its first background intensity replaced by the stated value and s.u. It is a display input, not a calculated reference.

The rendered gates inspect actual header and delegate cells in atoms, experiments, background, exclusions, preferred orientation and reflections. Numbering needs come from Qt text metrics on supplied two- and three-digit row counts, never the production width resolver. They change the viewport width, supply long keys, compare loop-table boundaries and create genuine overflow in both parameter consumers before inspecting the pixels beyond the input edge. Full-value editing remains a separate assertion.

The owner-behavior gates use the real Main window for sidebar borders, category activation, available Analysis height, input gaps, units, free-state presentation, chart cursors, examples and About navigation. The notices fixture is generated by `generate_notices.py` from the independently shipped THIRD-PARTY-NOTICES input. It never calls ApplicationInfo; every table attribution is compared with that frozen input. Existing CLI fit references supply the out-of-range values for table and standalone warning-tooltip checks.

Status inputs are supplied independently to actual delegates. The same cells are retained through fit-outcome, calculation and availability transitions; assertions inspect their drawn glyphs or rings, actual ink and word tooltips. The legacy declaration census remains a convention check only.

The JavaScript runner executes the real formatter functions and the actual StatusBar text, Repeater-model and Text bindings for running scans and completed summaries. The count-consumer escape test keeps the correct formatter but bypasses it in those bindings; both consumers must reject that mutation. Named colour tokens stand in for Qt style values; the actual FitOutcomes separator binding is executed too. Counts are inspected in the combined displayed text, so the verdict does not depend on how the Repeater splits its pieces. No formatter is copied. This source replay does not replace a GUI execution or the full published-SDK/source replay.

Round-2 geometry gates bound fixed columns from below as well as above. IDs fit the independently supplied longest short key and their heading, grow for a long key to the quarter-table cap, then shrink back when short keys return. Atom type, Wyckoff, glyph and ring ink fit their actual cell boundaries. `replay_boundary.py` copies the pinned gui-components archive and actual shared ListView into an isolated Qt runner directory. It executes the same observer and fit assertions as the page gates, with a no-clipping mutation and independent one-pixel ID, type, Wyckoff and action inputs. These are observer/shared-table controls, not a full feature-SDK or app replay.

The Analysis header vector comes from easydiffractionbeta v0.9.9 (`ec1d04ee36036dd092fdd8b779e99767afca6e5d`), `Fittables.qml`: name and units left; value, error, min and max right; numbering and vary inherit centered alignment. The delegate cells initially default to center, but gui-components v0.9.1 (`a573a9695e53a0807de197785e12f9facd06da05`) `TableView.qml` starts its width/alignment timer when content children change and assigns each cell its header's alignment. The settled delegate vector therefore matches the header vector. Edi's QML supplies neither expectation.

`replay_beta_alignment.py` exports those exact external commits and instantiates the actual Beta table, header and delegate declarations with supplied backend data. It records initial and settled row alignments and executes the hidden gate's alignment observer. The old centered oracle, a disabled assignment timer and an incorrect assignment in each column must reach the alignment refusal. Module names are adapted from EasyApp to EasyApplication; the alignment declarations and timer are retained. This reference-row replay is independent of edi's table implementation and does not stand in for a full app/SDK run.
